title: Schneckloth v. Bustamonte (1973)
key_points: Holding: Federally, consent must be voluntary under the totality of the circumstances; knowledge of the right to refuse is a factor but not required.
New Jersey: State v. Johnson, 68 N.J. 349 (1975) requires proof that the person knew they could refuse.
officer_notes: Scenario: During a stop you ask 'Mind if I look in the trunk?' and the driver says sure.
Takeaway: NJ is stricter; see State v. Johnson and State v. Carty.
